title: R5: Generic reuse, requirement profiles and templates
global_constraints: GC01: Script CEO owns dispatch, scheduling, gates, authoritative state, commits, and publication; no coordinating LLM is introduced.
GC02: The Codex path never executes OpenCode or silently changes runtime, model, reasoning effort, or role.
GC03: Every role receives explicit model and reasoning settings; operator, reviewer, and director have separate identities and permissions.
GC04: Plans, specs, prompts, ledger summaries, and implementation comments are English; product UI copy retains its established locale.
GC05: Codex workers inherit no brainstorming transcript; all required task context comes from versioned artifacts and explicit packages.
GC06: Operator-owned RED/GREEN and independent semantic review remain mandatory; mechanical green alone never approves a task or branch.
GC07: Raw evidence determines gates; RTK only changes the model-visible rendering and never the command exit code.
GC08: Unknown, malformed, stale, interrupted, or mismatched results never advance authoritative state.
GC09: Resume is confined to a recorded task family and role; unrelated tasks and closing use fresh contexts.
GC10: Parallel workers use distinct worktrees; shared plan writes, integration, and publication are serialized by scripts.
GC11: Existing user changes, unrelated branches, Codex sessions, credentials, and installed plugin caches are preserved.
GC12: Jev remains optional advisory inference; it cannot dispatch, select a tier, approve, route, or write the authoritative ledger.
GC13: Each new run confirms local-only or push-and-PR publication and concurrency at launch; resume retains those choices and no automatic merge is allowed.
GC14: Compatibility is claimed only for runtime/platform/toolchain combinations backed by the acceptance matrix.

tasks.title: Introduce applicable baseline requirement profiles
tasks.summary: Make structural product requirements explicit during planning without adding irrelevant features.
acceptance: Profiles declare identity/version/applicability, requirement IDs, acceptance checks, dependencies and opt-out reasons; resolve generic then ecosystem/category overlays with conflict detection.

Include input normalization, locale-aware masks, validation boundaries, accessible labels/errors/focus, loading/empty/error states, duplicate-submit prevention, retries, date/currency handling and secret-safe logging as applicable requirements.
Separate masks from validation; country-specific identifiers and payment rules require matching product scope. No automatic auth/payment/analytics features.
Planning emits selected requirements and exceptions into task acceptance before implementation. Unresolved conflicts ask a focused question, not silent precedence.
Test locale differences, non-UI tools, opted-out requirements, conflicting overlays, absent client/server boundaries and deterministic output.
Apply applicable defaults and present one consolidated requirements summary during brainstorming. Ask only about ambiguity/exceptions; do not silently add defaults or require approval for every item.

tasks.title: Build safe template repository and promotion workflows
tasks.summary: Package reviewed reusable assets with explicit repository configuration and publication authority.
acceptance: Use the confirmed separate private repository CarlosMonteiroNeto/code-templates. Keep remote provisioning as an explicit implementation action; this planning task creates no remote. Reuse an existing matching repository, validate ownership/visibility and do not silently publish client-specific material.
Scaffold profiles/templates/packages/catalog manifests in a named staging repository; exclude credentials, SQLite caches, embeddings and private project evidence.
Adoption success nominates promotion; explicit selection plus license/provenance/API/dependency/tests checks permits packaging. No TODO dependency versions or automatic publication.
Projects pin immutable release/commit and track local adaptations. Update preview compares changes; conflicts preserve local source and require user merge.
Promotion is idempotent by asset/version/source identity, refuses overwrite by default and records outcomes transactionally. Publication is a separate explicitly authorized operation.
Archive code is a reference only: implement current contracts with path traversal protection, dependency verification and duplicate-promotion fixtures.

tasks.title: Generalize research, dependency preparation and compatible adoption
tasks.summary: Expose generally useful Flutter-only lifecycle behavior through shared contracts and preserve ecosystem-specific implementation.
acceptance: Implement shared solution research records (requirement, alternatives, evidence, compatibility, license, selection/reason) and dependency preparation protocols using stage inventory ownership. Avoid additional agent dispatch for mechanical lookup or validation.
Preserve pub.dev/GitHub scoring semantics in Flutter adapters; generic callers consume evidence and do not apply Flutter numerical thresholds to every ecosystem.

Automatically adopt suitable templates when requirements/technical compatibility checks pass; raise questions only for changes/conflicts requiring judgment. Source score alone cannot authorize adoption. Stage material safely and preserve target project changes.

Allow new compatible, license-approved dependencies without separate user approval; unknown/conflicting checks ask the user. Acquire director-approved existing manifest/lockfile grants and coordinate writes through the shared resource lock before install.
Record versions, license/compatibility evidence, downloads/cache effects and source provenance. Keep secrets out of artifacts; never describe pub get as lockfile-only.

Keep RED/GREEN/review/RTK/final behavior routed to already shared owners. Generalize requirements and research entry points while leaving Flutter-specific UI/tooling in adapters; do not add a Graphify context stage or broaden the narrowly scoped R4 source-to-test impact adapter.

Fixtures prove generic operation without Flutter binaries when no Flutter capability applies, existing Flutter command compatibility, auto-adoption, ambiguous compatibility, dependency conflict and concurrent manifest claims.
